Welcome—I'm glad you're here.
Imagine a time before cities, before farming, before any of the rules we take for granted. Back then, human sexuality didn’t look much like what we expect today. Are you curious about how partnership, attraction, and desire might have unfolded in those ancient days?
That’s exactly what we’ll explore together, guided by the insights from Sex at Dawn: The Prehistoric Origins of Modern Sexuality by Christopher Ryan.
As we dive in, you’ll see how the stories of our evolutionary past challenge the idea that lifelong monogamy has always been our natural path. We’ll travel through anthropology, biology, and psychology, uncovering how our earliest ancestors—and even our primate cousins—experienced intimacy, cooperation, and a surprising degree of fluidity.
What if the ways we love and connect today are actually shaped by thousands of years of adaptation, rather than strict moral codes?
Along the way, we’ll question old beliefs about fidelity, jealousy, and gender roles, and see how the dance between social structures and sexual expression has influenced what we call “normal.”
So, get ready for a journey that invites all of us to look at human relationships with fresh eyes—because the more we understand where we come from, the better we can shape how we connect now.
